title: parse_header_typed_from: non-text headers round-trip through lossy UTF-8, silently corrupting non-ASCII bytes
description:
## Problem

In `mime-tree/src/header_typed.rs`, `parse_header_typed_from(header, form)` calls `header.value.as_bytes()` and feeds those bytes to `parse_header_typed`.

However, `header.value` for non-text headers was built via `String::from_utf8_lossy(raw_bytes)` in `extract_headers()` (`parse.rs`). Any non-ASCII bytes in the original raw header become U+FFFD (three UTF-8 bytes per replacement), so `header.value.as_bytes()` is not the original wire bytes — it is the lossy-converted bytes.

Callers who parse Addresses, MessageIds, or Date forms via the `ParsedHeader` convenience wrapper get silently different results from callers who call `parse_header_typed(form, raw_bytes)` directly with the original raw bytes.

## Concrete impact

A From: header containing ISO-8859-1 encoded display names (legal in RFC 5322 but not UTF-8) will have every high-byte replaced with U+FFFD. A name like `Fr\xe9d\xe9ric` becomes `Fr\xEF\xBF\xBDd\xEF\xBF\xBDric`. The address parser may then fail to parse the name at all or produce the replacement-character string.

## Files

- `mime-tree/src/parse.rs` — `extract_headers` constructs `header.value` with lossy conversion
- `mime-tree/src/header_typed.rs` — `parse_header_typed_from` uses `header.value.as_bytes()`

## What goes wrong if left as-is

Silent data loss for any non-UTF-8 From:/To:/Cc: headers. The callers of the JMAP adapter (crate-jmap-mime) that use the ParsedHeader-based convenience path will see garbled display names while direct callers using `parse_header_typed` with raw bytes see the correct original bytes. Callers have no way to know they are getting lossy results.
close_reason: Added raw_value to ParsedHeader, parse_header_typed_from now uses raw bytes. Two regression tests added.
